name: Fairfield County
seat: No county seat — county government abolished in 1960
population_source: 2020 U.S. Census (most populous county in Connecticut)

jurisdictions.name: Fairfield County
jurisdictions.governing_body: No county government — Connecticut abolished all county governments in 1960
jurisdictions.executive: None (services run by the towns and the state)

quorum_court.source: Connecticut abolished all eight county governments effective October 1, 1960 (Public Act 152). Fairfield County has no council, no commissioners, no county budget, and no county employees — it is a boundary for the courts only. Its 23 towns and the State of Connecticut provide all services; the Census Bureau now treats Connecticut’s regional planning Councils of Governments as the county-equivalents.

budget_adoption_window.note: There is no county budget; town budgets are adopted in the spring and the state budget by the General Assembly.

election_blackouts.note: Bright lines: no candidate issues, no active-ballot-measure issues, no named-individual conduct issues.
